messages:
ashwin: heads up — SOC asked for direct read access to the SIEM export bucket for triage. current plan was to keep exports encrypted with a customer KMS key and only allow the ingest role. thoughts?

taylor: do we mean direct S3 GET access or access via the ingest lambda?

ashwin: direct S3 GET. they want to run ad-hoc queries with Athena on raw exports sometimes.

phil: +1 to not giving direct GET unless we add strict controls. concerns: exfil risk, no timebound access, no MFA gating.

mia-soc: from SOC side — ad-hoc queries are rare but helpful. If we can provide time-limited creds or an audit proxy that streams results, that would work. Need to avoid friction during incidents. :hourglass_flowing_sand:

olivia: legal check: retention and e-discovery — if SOC can export or copy logs, retention SLAs could be violated. We need an audit trail and an approval flow.

ashwin: suggested approach: create a "siem-query-proxy" service that assumes a short-lived role and decrypts with KMS grants, returns only query results (no bulk object downloads). Role requests are JIT via Okta with approval scope. Thoughts on KMS config?

phil: KMS bits: we can use a grant for the proxy principal instead of changing key policy. grant looks like:
```bash
aws kms create-grant --key-id alias/logs-export-key --grantee-principal arn:aws:iam::123456789012:role/siem-query-proxy --operations Decrypt --constraints 'EncryptionContextSubset={"purpose":"siem-ingest"}'
```
This keeps the key policy tight and gives ephemeral permissions. Also enable CloudTrail KMS events for audit.

ashwin: perfect. then the proxy only has Decrypt on those ciphertexts. we should also require the proxy to call STS:AssumeRole with a session tag containing the requesting user so we can map actions.

olivia: add a required approval for anything that exceeds 30 days retention or if the query requests >1GB of raw data. also record the approval ticket id in the session tag.

mia-soc: ok, JIT with approval sounds fine. How do we handle RBAC for who can request JIT? SOC lead only?

phil: RBAC model: create a "security/analyst" group and a separate "security/lead" role. members of analyst can request, but requests auto-approve up to 100MB and 1 hour. anything beyond needs lead approval. enforce via the proxy.

ashwin: we also need to protect against misuse: add query result redaction rules (PII filters) and deny COPY/PUT operations. proxy must sanitize column names and strip base64 attachments.

olivia: legal: also require preservation holds if query is triggered as part of a legal matter. keep copies of query results in a WORM bucket with restricted access.

phil: implement S3 bucket policy deny for PutObject for the export prefixes from everyone except the ingest lambda role and the WORM archival role. sample policy snippet: 
```json
{"Version":"2012-10-17","Statement":[{"Effect":"Deny","Principal":"*","Action":"s3:PutObject","Resource":"arn:aws:s3:::redwood-logs/exports/*","Condition":{"StringNotEquals":{"aws:PrincipalArn":"arn:aws:iam::123456789012:role/ingest-lambda"}}}]
}
```
(we'll tighten Principals list)

ashwin: good. Also require S3 object lock on archival bucket.

mia-soc: operational ask — latency: we need these queries to be fast during incidents. Will proxy add too much overhead?

phil: proxy will stream results and cache recent query results for 15 minutes. we should be fine. Continuous batching for big queries.

taylor: integration note: Athena won't be able to read encrypted objects unless proxy supplies decrypted stream. We can either let proxy materialize queryable table using Parquet in an internal bucket (encrypted with same key) or implement a DecryptWrapper for Athena. The Parquet path is simpler.

ashwin: prefer Parquet transform — smaller, cheaper, and searchable. Make transform job write to internal-parquet-bucket with server-side encryption KMS. Access to that bucket limited to proxy and analytics roles.

olivia: retention policy question: security events retention currently 1 year, compliance wants 7 years for certain audit logs. We need classification per prefix.

phil: agree. tag exports with metadata: "retention:1y|7y". lifecycle policies can move older data to glacier. But archival with >1y must be write-once with object lock if legal requirement.

mia-soc: can we get a simple UI in Console to request JIT and see approvals? that would reduce Slack pings.

ashwin: yep — I'll create a tiny console flow that hits the proxy request API and records approvals in Dynamo with the ticket id.

deploy-bot: deployment started for branch feature/siem-proxy-reqs (PR #412) — smoke tests: integration-staging.

ashwin: ok i'll pair with @taylor on the proxy PR. Next steps: 1) phil to write KMS grant playbook + CloudTrail filters; 2) olivia to draft retention & legal hold rules; 3) taylor to prototype parquet transform; 4) mia to define SOC autoprov limits.

phil: I'll drop the playbook doc in #eng-security/docs later today.

olivia: I'll open a quick legal checklist ticket.

mia-soc: will compile SOC requirements and share sample queries.

ashwin: thanks all — let's aim to have an MVP gated for oncall in two weeks. :rocket:
